The test image shows a **banana leaf** with:
- Large yellow/tan area in the center
- Multiple dark brown/black spots scattered throughout the yellowed region
- Green healthy tissue visible on both sides

This pattern (chlorosis + dark spots on leaf) points to either Yellow_And_Black_Sigatoka or Cordana_Leaf_Spot. I'll use my one reference image view on Yellow_And_Black_Sigatoka since the extensive yellowing with black spots matches its symptom profile.

**Analysis:**

The reference image for Yellow_And_Black_Sigatoka shows large necrotic brown areas with yellow borders along the leaf — consistent with advanced Sigatoka infection.

Comparing to the test image:
- Test image: large yellow/tan area with many scattered dark brown-black spots, green margins — this matches an advanced Sigatoka stage where multiple lesions have coalesced, causing broad chlorosis dotted with black necrotic foci
- The symptom description confirms: "chlorotic flecking," "black spots," reduced photosynthesis from extensive leaf damage
- The pattern does not resemble Cordana Leaf Spot (which shows distinct oval lesions with gray centers and defined dark borders) or Panama Disease (which shows overall leaf wilt/yellowing without discrete spots)
